HAL_TIM_UpdateCallback is weak and may be implemented in a user file.

RM0522 p382 explicitly supports memory/peripheral in all four source/destination combinations; per-channel completion/half/error/suspend events. This is hardware support, not proof of arbitrary endpoint safety or dual handshakes.
RM0522 Table86: C53xxx/C542xx have four channels0..3 on each LPDMA1/2; larger variants differ. All LPDMA instances/channels connect the same supported request/trigger set. LPDMA has no FIFO.
RM0522 Table90: SPI1 RX/TX request selectors4/5 and I2C1 RX/TX10/11. LPDMA2 has no FIFO. Request selection alone does not prove peripheral presence on every part.
RM0522 Table90: USART2 RX/TX selectors14/15; channel request availability must be intersected with exact part presence.

RM0522 Table91 lists only lptim1_ue_dma as block request. Table92 PFREQ early termination is limited to channels0/7; combining this with C542 channel presence in Table86 leaves channel0 on each controller.
RM0522 linked-list base/address rules require all linked-list nodes in the same64Kbyte address window. Linked-list execution is documented, not implemented by the direct-transfer cards.
RM0522 source/destination widths support1/2/4 bytes;8-byte width is not supported. Source/destination addresses must align to respective widths; increment is contiguous or fixed.
RM0522 supports padding/truncation/sign extension between widths, not packing multiple source cells. Current direct-transfer implementation domain uses equal widths only.

RM0522 prohibits the same active peripheral request on multiple active channels without automatic error detection. SWREQ1 generates software requests; with SWREQ0 the first memory read is gated by the selected hardware request whether the peripheral is source or destination. The described request mechanism does not establish arbitrary endpoint-pair readiness.
RM0522 documents four priority levels with arbitration per single atomic read/write transfer. Priority does not certify an application latency or bandwidth.
RM0522 describes circular buffering using a linked-list reload of block size and memory address. Direct-transfer cards are finite blocks and do not implement circular mode.
RM0522 documents separate enable bits/flags for channel completion, half completion, data/user/link/trigger errors and suspend; event flag state is separate from interrupt enable.

RM0522 channel privilege controls source/destination/link accesses; data-transfer errors stop the channel and require channel reset before reuse. Bus reachability alone does not establish access rights.
RM0522 trigger overrun flag does not automatically disable the channel. Direct cards do not enable hardware triggers; triggered profiles need explicit overrun handling.
RM0522 CBR1 BNDT source-byte count is16bits; a nonzero count must be a multiple of source width or a user-setting error occurs.

RM0522 p89 LPDMA bus targets Flash, SRAM1/2 and AHB peripheral bridges. This family bus statement does not establish all peripherals, security/privilege settings, cache coherence or any arbitrary address on C542.
ES0676 Rev2 applicability includes STM32C531/532/542; actual silicon cut must be identified, not inferred from board name.
ES0676 I2C setup-time limitation: minimum input clocks4/10/20MHz for Standard/Fast/Fast-mode-plus under documented setup-time assumptions. Electrical timing remains a board requirement.
ES0676 I2C controller spurious BERR workaround is clear flag only, no transfer abort. USART auto-baud/ONEBIT restrictions are separate; current profile disables these modes.
ES0676 SPI slave RDY-output high-clock limitation is outside master/internal-NSS profile; not a complete SPI system qualification.
HAL2 direct-transfer struct has request, direction, source/destination increment and widths, priority; widths byte/halfword/word. Enum names alone do not characterize P2P silicon support.
HAL2 names the SPI1/I2C1/USART2 RX/TX requests on LPDMA1; exact part presence established separately.
HAL2 exposes equivalent LPDMA2 SPI1/I2C1/USART2 request constants, independently from channel allocation.
HAL2 direct config writes source/destination controls; non-M2M chooses request, direction controls software-request mode. No second endpoint handshake is configured.
LL direction values map memory-to-memory to SWREQ; peripheral-to-memory zero and memory-to-peripheral alias it. Do not infer silicon endpoint restrictions from HAL enum spelling.
HAL2 exposes direct and peripheral-direct configuration entry points and explicit flow-control/trigger configuration APIs. These declarations alone do not establish reset state.
HAL2 exposes start with byte count, abort, IRQ dispatch and per-handle completion/error/abort callbacks. Error-code query is gated by USE_HAL_DMA_GET_LAST_ERRORS.
HAL RCC exposes LPDMA1/2 clock enable and disable APIs.
Exact STM32C542xx header declares LPDMA1/2 channel0..3 IRQs and I2C1/SPI1/USART2 IRQ enum values; names are used only for literal declaration binding.
STM32C542xx header declares eight physical channel instances; controller2 channel resources must not alias controller1 resources.
Captured foundation selects HAL DMA, LL DMA and HAL Q components plus UART; DMA source is already selected, no extra DMA CMake insertion required.
SDK CMake includes stm32c5xx_hal_dma.c for the already-selected HAL DMA component; do not compile it twice.
Pinned official C542 uart example explicitly configures pins, clocks, direct byte DMA, handle links and IRQs. Example channel0/1 choices are not fixed hardware routing restrictions.
Official uart example IRQ definitions dispatch selected peripheral and channel handlers; application must use manifest-selected physical channels.
Pinned official C542 i2c example explicitly configures pins, clocks, direct byte DMA, handle links and IRQs. Example channel0/1 choices are not fixed hardware routing restrictions.
Official i2c example IRQ definitions dispatch selected peripheral and channel handlers; application must use manifest-selected physical channels.
Pinned official C542 spi example explicitly configures pins, clocks, direct byte DMA, handle links and IRQs. Example channel0/1 choices are not fixed hardware routing restrictions.
Official spi example IRQ definitions dispatch selected peripheral and channel handlers; application must use manifest-selected physical channels.
HAL2 SetTxDMA/SetRxDMA allows configured/init handles in idle/reset transfer state; reuse the initialized USART2 handle while idle.
HAL2 UART receive completion callback takes handle, size_byte and rx_event; TX/error/abort callbacks have handle only.
HAL2 finite UART DMA APIs take byte counts; abort APIs act through the peripheral handle.
Direct UART DMA TX complete enables USART TC interrupt; DMA completion alone is not UART wire completion. USART IRQ must remain enabled.
HAL2 controller DMA APIs use byte counts and separate event/error handlers; provides TX/RX/memory completion/error/abort callbacks.
HAL2 mode enum explicitly distinguishes MASTER, SLAVE, MASTER_MEM and NONE. BERR workaround is scoped to sampled master modes, preserving other error handling.
HAL2 controller DMA documentation requires7bit target address shifted left; master transfer sets handle mode MASTER.
Upstream HAL2 I2C error handler sends BERR to I2C_ITError; using this unchanged conflicts with ES0676 controller clear-only workaround.

The SPI header declares DMA transfers with count_packet, raw abort APIs, SPI IRQ/callbacks, per-handle callback registration under USE_HAL_SPI_REGISTER_CALLBACKS, GetState, and GetLastErrorCodes under USE_HAL_SPI_GET_LAST_ERRORS. These declarations are not physical quiescence or hardware compatibility proof.
SPI direct full-duplex DMA completion enables peripheral EOT IRQ; SPI peripheral IRQ is required for final completion.
Exact mapped pinout declares GPIOA user_gpio on PA4; independent output can be allocated for external device select without cloning SPI pins.
Exact mapped package bonds PA4 to package position20.

HAL_GPIO_Init accepts port, pin mask and configuration; for output mode it writes p_config->init_state before configuring output speed/type/pull/mode, then returns HAL_OK. A prior WritePin is therefore not a substitute for setting init_state. External electrical safety is a separate obligation.
Version2 implementation domains, conservative physical ownership/adoption policy and explicit unknowns. This is BKPT engineering policy, not a manufacturer concurrency/electrical specification.
Exact mapped pinout declares I2C1_SCL on PB6 using AF4.
Exact mapped pinout declares I2C1_SDA on PB7 using AF4.
Exact mapped pinout declares SPI1_MISO on PA6 using AF5.
Exact mapped pinout declares SPI1_MOSI on PA7 using AF5.
Exact mapped pinout declares SPI1_SCK on PA5 using AF5.
HAL2 DMA initialization associates a selected physical channel, initializes default callbacks and state; optional clock-enable behavior is configured separately.

HAL_DMA_DeInit disables and clears only the selected physical channel, resets CCR/CTR1/CTR2/CBR1/CLLR and sets software RESET state. GetLLInstance exposes the selected channel for the explicit active-channel check; it is not a controller-wide reset.
LL_DMA_IsEnabledChannel reads the selected physical channel CCR.EN bit. BKPT setup rejects an enabled channel before deinitializing it; no takeover of an ongoing transfer is implemented.
HAL2 direct DMA configuration consumes the explicit request, direction, increment, width and priority fields; allowed INIT/IDLE states are debug assertions.
LPDMA1 SPI1 RX/TX selectors are 4/5, I2C1 10/11 and USART2 14/15 in this exact SDK.
LPDMA2 explicitly uses the same six numeric SPI1/I2C1/USART2 selectors as LPDMA1 in this exact SDK; this is not a cross-family claim.
HAL2 forwards the explicit request enum numeric value to LL_DMA_SetPeriphRequest without a controller-specific remapping.
The request member is hal_dma_request_source_t. Direct configuration enumerates direction, increment, data widths and priority.
NVIC exposes exact priority, pending-clear and enable calls; priority 5 is a BKPT engineering policy, not a manufacturer-required priority.
Per-handle UART callback registration declarations are guarded by USE_HAL_UART_REGISTER_CALLBACKS.
UART completion callback registration requires configured/init global state and BOTH TX/RX idle/reset via debug assertions. NULL is rejected only with parameter checking enabled.
UART per-handle abort/error callback registration has the same idle/reset state requirements; return success does not validate runtime state when assertions are disabled.
UART exposes TX/RX state queries used by the adopted-handle initialization runtime guard.

The I2C handle typedef, void(hal_i2c_handle_t*) callback typedef and per-handle MASTER transfer/error/abort registration declarations are present; callback types/registration are guarded by USE_HAL_I2C_REGISTER_CALLBACKS. Other APIs inside this locator are not additional reviewed operation claims.
HAL2 I2C documents callback registration only in INIT or IDLE, not while a transfer or abort is active.
HAL2 SPI per-handle TX/RX/TxRx, error and abort registration APIs require USE_HAL_SPI_REGISTER_CALLBACKS.
HAL2 SPI documents callback registration only in INIT or IDLE; initialization restores defaults.

HAL_UART_Abort disables UART request gates and invokes linked DMA abort but ignores its return; UART IDLE/HAL_OK alone do not confirm physical DMA quiescence.
UART_Abort disables selected UART interrupts and clears listed flags; it does not confirm DMA completion.
DMA blocking abort can return HAL_ERROR for already idle or timeout. Timeout may leave software ABORT; only physical IDLE plus EN0 establishes disabled, with software IDLE required for reuse.
Asynchronous DMA abort is distinct from confirmation; already idle returns HAL_ERROR. Caller must not infer active failure or completion solely from return.
LL_DMA_IsEnabledChannel reads the selected CCR.EN bit.
LL_DMA_IsActiveFlag_IDLE observes the selected channel physical CSR.IDLEF.
RM0522 p426 IDLE includes a suspended channel; IDLE alone is not disabled proof.
RM0522 p428 distinguishes suspended IDLE1/EN1 from disabled IDLE1/EN0 and documents reset and EN transitions.
USART DMA RX request enabled state is read from CR3.DMAR.
USART DMA TX request enabled state is read from CR3.DMAT.
CMSIS NVIC_GetEnableIRQ reads enable state; DisableIRQ clears only that IRQ and executes DSB/ISB.
CMSIS pending clear is IRQ-specific; it does not clear peripheral sources.
HAL_CORTEX_NVIC_DisableIRQ delegates to the CMSIS NVIC_DisableIRQ implementation.
LL_DMA_ClearFlag clears explicitly selected channel flags through CFCR.
CMSIS DSB waits for explicit preceding memory accesses to complete; not a replacement for peripheral quiescence checks.
IPSR reads exception number; zero denotes Thread mode under the ARM execution model.
CMSIS reads PRIMASK interrupt mask; UART helper rejects masked blocking waits.
CMSIS reads BASEPRI priority mask; helper rejects nonzero mask before a blocking SysTick-based wait.
CMSIS reads FAULTMASK; helper rejects masked waits.
HAL timer formula and prescaler/period domains; repetition0 gives frequency=TIM_CLK/((PSC+1)*(ARR+1)).
HAL SetConfig writes exact ARR/PSC and generates update to load prescaler; sets software IDLE.
HAL_TIM_Start_IT requires IDLE and transitions to ACTIVE before enabling update interrupt/counter.
HAL_TIM_Stop_IT disables timer interrupts and counter and sets software IDLE.
HAL_TIM_RegisterUpdateCallback installs per-handle update callback; parameter checking is build-dependent.
Per-handle timer callback type is void(hal_tim_handle_t*) under USE_HAL_TIM_REGISTER_CALLBACKS.
LL update generation writes TIM_EGR.UG; counter/reset semantics are established separately by RM0522.
RM0522 p1277 UG reinitializes timer counter and clears prescaler counter without changing the ratio.
RM0522 p1263 update/URS/UDIS semantics and prescaler preload behavior; generated component uses reset profile and clears UIF before start.
BKPT exact nominal frequency domain derived from pinned144MHz profile and conservative register limits; independently enumerated arithmetic, not measured hardware timing.
I2C controller abort initiates STOP and asynchronous completion, not immediate quiescence.
I2C error/abort path disables DMA requests and dispatches asynchronous DMA abort; missing STOP/IRQ completion cannot be assumed released.

SPI blocking abort propagates nested DMA failures and sets software IDLE even on error. Its raw return/software IDLE alone cannot establish physical DMA quiescence. Interrupt-mode abort installs DMA abort callbacks before calling HAL_DMA_Abort_IT; an already-idle DMA error does not clear those pointers, and dma_used suppresses the synchronous close path.

In the pinned full-duplex DMA implementation, <=8bit frames pass count_packet as the DMA byte count; 9-16bit and wider frames multiply it. The selected authored template configures 8bit frames.
Exact callback typedef declarations and USE_HAL_UART_REGISTER_CALLBACKS guard.
Literal RX event enumeration: transfer-complete TC=0U; other enum members are not half-complete events.
Finite direct DMA full completion reports rx_xfer_size and TC through the registered RX completion callback; half completion dispatches a separate one-argument callback.
UART_EndTransmit_IT sets software TX idle and dispatches the registered final TX callback.
Ordinary HAL_UART_Transmit_DMA starts with the explicit HAL_UART_OPT_DMA_TX_IT_HT option.
TX DMA start passes the half-transfer interrupt option and assigns UART_DMATxHalfCplt as the DMA half callback.
The half DMA callback dispatches the distinct one-argument registered UART TX-half callback, or legacy callback when registration is disabled.
Callback initialization explicitly installs HAL_UART_TxHalfCpltCallback, described by the pinned source as Legacy weak TxHalfCpltCallback.
Enabled USART TC interrupt calls UART_EndTransmit_IT.
State getters read handle software fields; GetLastErrorCodes is guarded and returns the bitwise OR of stored RX/TX error codes.
Pinned HAL enable requires software IDLE, disables PE, calls the LL FMP enable, sets PE enabled and returns HAL_OK. The component checks its status before downstream setup.
Pinned LL implementation sets/clears/reads CR1.FMP; comments identify its I/O-drive purpose. No quantitative current guarantee is inferred without the datasheet conditions.
RM0522 printed1673: CR1 reset value is0 and bit24 selects FMP I/O drive. This is not asserted to be an unconditional digital1MHz gate.

DS15135 printed44 identifies PB6/PB7 as FT_f; printed89 scopes Fm+ I/O current support to FT_f and requires proper configuration. Actual supply/load, pullups and electrical timing remain unverified; no quantitative current or VOL promise.
BKPT-authored resource-bound implementation template; not manufacturer hardware evidence.
GPIO port, selected output mode/type/speed/pull, pin-state and configuration types are declared, including init_state; PA4/PA5 pin masks are declared. These declarations do not prove external wiring.
HAL_GPIO_Init returns hal_status_t and accepts a const configuration; HAL_GPIO_WritePin and HAL_GPIO_TogglePin return void. Their port argument is hal_gpio_t and pin selection is a uint32_t mask.
HAL_RCC_GPIOA_EnableClock is a zero-argument static-inline void function enabling GPIOA through the LL AHB2 clock gate.
stm32_hal.h includes stm32c5xx_hal_gpio.h when USE_HAL_GPIO_MODULE is defined and equals 1; this guarded include provides the selected GPIO types and declarations.
BKPT-authored resource-bound SPI implementation artifact; not manufacturer hardware evidence.
BKPT-authored resource-bound SPI implementation artifact; not manufacturer hardware evidence.
SPI IRQ errors disable SPI/request gates and start HAL_DMA_Abort_IT with SPI_DMAAbortOnError callbacks; the DMA branch does not synchronously set SPI IDLE.

SPI_DMAError and SPI_DMAAbortOnError call SPI_CloseTransfer/error callback. TX/RX user-abort completion callbacks clear their own abort callback pointer and wait for the peer pointer to clear before closing SPI.

Synchronous SPI_AbortTransfer disables SPI/IRQs/request gates and clears flags/counts without invoking callbacks; SPI_CloseTransfer can set IDLE without stopping either DMA channel. FAULT is preserved by CloseTransfer.
LL_SPI_Disable clears CR1.SPE; LL_SPI_IsEnabled reads the selected SPI SPE bit.
LL_SPI_GetMode reads CFG2.MASTER and LL_SPI_IsActiveMasterTransfer reads CR1.CSTART. Unrelated APIs within the locator are not additional reviewed claims.
LL SPI DMA request getters read the selected SPI CFG1 RXDMAEN/TXDMAEN bits.
SPI_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT is 100; blocking abort uses three SystemCoreClock-scaled counter loops with that nominal budget, not a hard elapsed-time guarantee.
DMA_SUSPEND_TIMEOUT is 1 millisecond; blocking abort compares the live HAL tick difference against this threshold.
DMA SUSP interrupt handling resets an ABORT channel, disables its interrupts, sets software IDLE and invokes its abort callback; ordinary suspension instead becomes SUSPEND.
BKPT authored finite-operation implementation artifact; not manufacturer hardware evidence.
Master DMA TX initializes ISR/state before DMA start; DMA-start failure resets state/mode but leaves the ISR pointer. A zero length takes an interrupt transfer path.
Master DMA RX selects callbacks and the DMA channel, then enables the request gate; start failure may leave the ISR pointer while mode/state revert.
Master Abort_IT sets ABORT and requests STOP/interrupt completion; successful initiation does not prove quiescence.
I2C_ITError clears mode/ISR and may initiate linked DMA abort based on previous_state. Error/abort callbacks are distinct from physical DMA release.
Master DMA completion disables its request gate and may enable STOP/TC interrupts; DMA completion alone is not peripheral transaction completion.
Event IRQ dispatch calls the current transfer ISR only if the pointer is non-null.
LL_I2C_DisableIT clears selected CR1 interrupt enables. IsEnabledIT tests all selected bits, not whether any selected bit is set.
Direct interrupt transfer start configures addresses/size, enables interrupts and the channel; assertions specify finite size and valid states.
Abort_IT accepts IDLE/ACTIVE, requests asynchronous suspend if physically active; already-idle returns error after setting software IDLE. No buffer-release inference from that return alone.
Master complete handles NACK errors/abort and clears mode and transfer ISR before successful completion callbacks.
Error IRQ dispatch collects error flags and calls I2C_ITError. The inherited exact BERR workaround is a separate integration edit.
Master DMA ISR processes STOP/NACK and transfer-count conditions; short finite operations avoid reload DMA restarts.
Error callback helper transitions ABORT to IDLE before abort completion notification, otherwise reports error.
DMA abort completion delegates to I2C_TreatErrorCallback through the parent handle.
DMA error handling resets channel and sets IDLE for transfer errors; trigger overrun alone does not reset the channel. Error notification is not general buffer release proof.

Reusable existing USART2 polling endpoint. After successful mx_system_init(), include mx_usart2.h and obtain hal_uart_handle_t *uart=mx_usart2_uart_gethandle(); do not initialize a second USART2 handle. Captured setup enables USART2/GPIOA, selects PCLK1 and PA2 TX/PA3 RX AF7, 115200 8N1, no flow control, oversampling 16 and one-bit sampling disabled. Only baud_rate 115200 is in this input domain.
HAL_UART_Transmit(uart,data,size_byte,timeout_ms) and HAL_UART_Receive(uart,data,size_byte,timeout_ms) block; check returned hal_status_t and use bounded application-appropriate timeouts. Polling needs no UART IRQ or DMA-channel allocation. Do not block inside timer callbacks. If basic_stdio is used, serialize it with direct traffic: BASIC_STDIO_UART_GETHANDLE maps to this handle. UART HAL/LL/generated source/config are included; no edit needed. Pack-declared HAL DMA dependency does not allocate a hardware DMA channel. Other baud/framing, IRQ/DMA, auto-baud, low-power and electrical/VCP behavior remain outside coverage; complete ES0676 applicability is not certified.

Materialization owns persistent DMA handle setup, selected controller clock enables, direct-transfer configuration, handle links and IRQ dispatch through capability components. Preserve generated files and startup calls; do not create duplicate handles or vector handlers or reset a shared controller. HAL peripheral drivers own their linked DMA callbacks. Application registers peripheral callbacks, keeps SysTick, checks every operation status and implements bounded completion/error/abort handling outside IRQ callbacks. SRAM buffers remain live and unmodified until completion or confirmed abort. Blocks are finite 1..65535 bytes with equal widths; linked/circular operation is not implemented. Allocation and compilation do not validate pointer bounds/alignment, MPU/cache/privilege, throughput or wiring.

Materialization now emits and links persistent initialization, a typed handle accessor and owned IRQ handlers. Preserve the generated includes and init calls after mx_system_init. Initialization is one-shot/fail-stop; application owns callback registration, transfers, timeouts and confirmed abort handling. Generated component provides a persistent configured memory-to-memory DMA handle and selected IRQ dispatch; use its returned interface. It increments both addresses with equal selected width1/2/4. Register per-handle HAL_DMA_RegisterXferCpltCallback, HAL_DMA_RegisterXferErrorCallback and HAL_DMA_RegisterXferAbortCallback (void callback(hal_dma_handle_t*)). Call HAL_DMA_StartDirectXfer_IT(h,(uint32_t)src,(uint32_t)dst,length_bytes) and check status. Planner validates length1..65535 and width divisibility; application must check actual aligned addresses, sufficient nonoverlapping DMA-accessible SRAM buffers and no concurrent modification. On timeout, HAL_DMA_Abort HAL_OK confirms its successful blocking path. HAL_ERROR may mean already idle or failed abort: without independent software IDLE plus physical IDLE1/EN0 proof, fail-stop and retain buffers. Async abort needs confirmed completion; no automatic reuse on timeout. Error notification alone is not confirmed abort. Read HAL_DMA_GetLastErrorCodes. No circular reload, cache maintenance or arbitrary MMIO readiness guarantee.

interface.lifecycle: Use the generated header. bkpt_op_result has state, reason, buffers_released. States: READY, ACTIVE, STOPPING, DONE, FAILED, UNSAFE (prefix BKPT_OP_). Reasons: NO_ERROR, IO_ERROR, TIMEOUT, CANCELLED, START_ERROR (prefix BKPT_OP_). DONE permits the next start; FAILED/UNSAFE are terminal, no retry/rearm. buffers_released is true only READY/DONE/FAILED; never reuse on STOPPING/UNSAFE.
interface.timing: Pass monotonically wrapping uint32 millisecond now and timeout/recovery in 1..INT32_MAX ms; call poll regularly from the sole foreground owner with interrupts unmasked. Deadlines are observed, not hard real time. Error wins over timeout; completion first observed at deadline is timeout. Proven quiescence at recovery deadline releases as FAILED, otherwise UNSAFE permanently retains buffers. No waiting inside poll/cancel.
interface.ownership: start returns 0 when ownership was accepted, including an underlying HAL-start failure reported by poll; nonzero refuses without new ownership. Check every start and poll. Owns all callbacks/handles/IRQs; no raw accessors or callback registration. ISR/masked-context calls are rejected or return the current snapshot without progress. Buffers stay live until buffers_released; application must check size, DMA accessibility and cache/MPU requirements.
